chunks: Mu‘āwiyah ibn ‘Ammār asked Abā ‘Abdillāh عليه السلام
about a man from the people of al-Madīnah who entered into ihram from al-Juḥfah
So he said: “There is no harm.”

key_terms.أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: Imam Ja‘far al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام, the one giving the ruling
key_terms.أَحْرَمَ: Entered into the state of ihram for hajj or ‘umrah
key_terms.الْجُحْفَةِ: A miqat location from which ihram may be assumed
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no harm; it is permissible
key_terms.مُعَاوِيَةُ بْنُ عَمَّارٍ: A transmitter who asked the Imam about this ruling

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a person from Madinah to assume ihram from al-Juhfah?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding ihram for a person from al-Madīnah who entered ihram from al-Juḥfah. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام states that there is no problem in doing so, indicating its permissibility in this case.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2527 - Mu‘awiyah ibn Ammar asked Abu Abdullah (as)
about a man from Medina who assumed Ihram from Al-Juhfa.
